item.title: Author Event: Jon Else — Thu Sep 24, 6:30 PM — The Avid Reader
item.description: Jon Else @ The Avid Reader Thursday Sep 24th, 2026 | 6:30 PM – 7:30 PM About the Book – Frenchman Flat: The Rise and Fall of Atomic Bombs The story of a single nuclear bomb’s deep origins, brief life during the Cold War, and lasting environmental and political legacies—as a fresh path to consider the entire sweep of the American nuclear enterprise. A grave reminder of the frightening truth about nuclear testing, as international norms waver. As the US and Russia let one treaty after another falter and expire, this urgent book reminds us of the price of those tests. Frenchman Flat recounts the science, politics, and human experience of those who developed nuclear weapons, suffered the consequences, and fought for and against arms control between the 1940s and 1990s. The throughline of this vast, complex story is a 37-kiloton atomic bomb dubbed “Priscilla” that was exploded above a custom-built mini-civilization at Frenchman Flat, Nevada, in 1957. Jon Else uses Priscilla and the bombs

item.title: Let’s Talk Murder! Mystery Authors Discuss Their Work — Thu Sep 24, 7:00 PM — Winters Community Library
item.description: From cozy village mysteries to dark psychological thrillers, mystery novels are perennially popular: studied by academics, promoted by celebrities, and discussed in book clubs worldwide. What is the draw of these stories, combining logical deduction and atmospheric dread? Winters Friends of the Library invites everyone to learn more at a special author talk with three award-winning mystery writers. Catriona McPherson, Jennifer K. Morita, and Laura Jensen Walker will share insights on their writing lives and the mystery genre. Whether you are an avid mystery reader or new to the genre, it will be fascinating to hear what these authors have to say about the challenges and pleasures of writing mysterious fiction. Following the talk, attendees may enjoy refreshments and chat with the authors and fellow readers. Books will be available for purchase and signing. item.title: Davis Waldorf School's Parent & Child Class — Fri Sep 25, 10:00 AM — Davis Waldorf School
item.description:
The first three years in a child’s life are an amazing time of growth that fill parents and caregivers with awe and wonder. Parent & Child classes are held in a warm and welcoming environment that is carefully arranged for creative play in our Buttercup Preschool room. This program offers the very young child freedom to explore within loving boundaries, and teaches parents/caregivers about Waldorf education’s many benefits. Classes are led by an experienced Early Childhood educator and echo the rhythms of the Waldorf preschool. Additionally, classes offer caregivers a place to connect about child development and parenting techniques. We welcome caregivers of all kinds—parents, grandparents, nannies—to join our sessions!
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

Most importantly, participants will learn about the open access publishing support available through the University of California libraries consortium and UC Davis Library.

item.title: Workshop: Organize, Cite, Publish: Citation Management from First Search to Final Draft — Fri Oct 30, 12:00 PM — Walker Hall
item.description:
Keep your sources, notes, PDFs, and citations organized from your first search through your final draft. In this workshop, we'll explore strategies for managing research throughout the literature review and publication process using citation management tools. Discover efficient ways to import, organize and tag sources, annotate PDFs, and generate citations and bibliographies. Come learn the tools and workflows that can save you time—and make your thesis advisor a little envious.
Register:
Zoom Registration
In-Person Registration
Source: UC Davis Library

item.title: Workshop: Mastering Your Literature Search: Techniques, Tools and AI — Fri Nov 6, 12:00 PM — Walker Hall
item.description:
This workshop is ideal for any student or researcher embarking on a literature search or review, or anyone wanting to learn about emerging AI tools for literature searching. The session will cover (1) how to translate your research question into a search strategy that will uncover the scholarly literature you need, (2) the library tools you will need for your searches, and (3) an introduction to the AI tools designed for literature searching and how they can supplement your search strategy.
Register:
Zoom Registration
In-Person Registration
Source: UC Davis Library

item.title: Workshop: So you’re ready to publish your first scientific paper?... — Fri Nov 13, 12:00 PM — Walker Hall
item.description:
Publishing research in a scientific journal is a critical step in every researcher's journey. However, it can be a very complex and intimidating landscape when doing it for the first time. This workshop will provide an introduction to major parts of the process including, an overview of the scientific publishing landscape, selecting a journal, working with collaborators, and more! This workshop is aimed at all STEM-aligned fields and all experience levels, but beginners are especially welcome.

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Wed Sep 23, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p

item.title: DJUSD Board Meetings — Thu Dec 3, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
DJUSD Board meetings offer insight on how the school district remains responsive to the community’s values, beliefs, and priorities. The Board meetings occur on every first and third Thursday, in the City of Davis Community Chambers. 23 Russell Boulevard. Public session starts at 6:30 PM. Meetings are cablecast live on Channel 17 (Comcast) or streamed on the DJUSD-TV website.
The Davis Joint Unified School District’s Board of Education is comprised of five community members, responsible for setting district policy, approving the budget, and hiring the superintendent for schools in Davis, California. The agendas for the meetings are posted at least 72 hours in advance.
For more information on special meetings, agendas, public comment, and more, visit the DJUSD Board site.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year) — Wed Dec 9, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
The Davis Farmers Market continues every Wednesday in Central Park with new fall hours! Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. Wednesday Market Details:

item.title: Grounded Together: Building Resilience, Connection, and Community — Wed Sep 23, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community ***P.S. this is part of a 5 week series, though not required, you are highly encouraged to attend all - No meeting on Oct 7***
Join **Rev. Rola Al-Ashkar** for a five-week journey exploring how our life experiences shape the way we respond to stress, conflict, belonging, and relationships. Through storytelling, guided reflection, and gentle body-centered (somatic) practices, participants will develop tools for greater self-awareness, emotional resilience, and compassionate listening. Whether you're seeking personal growth, healthier relationships, or a deeper sense of connection within our community, this series offers a welcoming and supportive space. No prior experience is necessary. Please register using the following link: [[LINK](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdxWVImvnFcRLw5on8gH2WFGQfoMnVmNowpxZd9FHajblr2Iw/viewform?usp=send_form)]. **Wednesdays:** Sept. 16, 23, 30; Oct. 14 & 21 6:00 – 8:00 pm
